topic.subject: social
topic.title: The making of a global world
topic.scope: Silk routes, food travels, rinderpest, indentured labour, Great Depression, Bretton Woods

misconceptions.statement: Globalisation is a modern phenomenon that only started with the internet and airplanes.
misconceptions.why: Students conflate the modern digital era with the historical process of global interconnectedness.
misconceptions.fix: Globalisation has existed for centuries through the movement of goods, people, and ideas along ancient trade routes.

probe.question: Did global exchange exist before the 20th century?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because there was no technology to connect countries.

misconceptions.statement: Food items like potatoes and chillies have always been grown in India.
misconceptions.why: Students assume that common dietary staples are native to their own geography due to long-term cultural integration.
misconceptions.fix: Many common Indian foods were introduced from the Americas by explorers and traders after the 15th century.

probe.question: Where did potatoes originate?
probe.wrong_answer: They are native to India and have been grown here since ancient times.

misconceptions.statement: Indentured labourers were essentially the same as modern-day migrant workers who choose their jobs.
misconceptions.why: Students fail to distinguish between voluntary migration and the coercive, contract-based system of the colonial era.
misconceptions.fix: Indentured labour was a system of unfree labour where workers were bound by harsh contracts and often deceived about their working conditions.

probe.question: Why did people sign up for indentured labour?
probe.wrong_answer: They were looking for better job opportunities and higher wages abroad.

concepts.name: The Great Depression and Global Economy

misconceptions.statement: The Great Depression was caused solely by the stock market crash in the USA.
misconceptions.why: Textbooks often highlight the 1929 crash as the primary event, leading students to ignore structural economic factors.
misconceptions.fix: The Depression resulted from a combination of overproduction, agricultural crisis, and the fragility of the international banking system.

probe.question: What was the main cause of the Great Depression?
probe.wrong_answer: The stock market crash in America was the only reason the whole world suffered.

misconceptions.statement: The IMF and World Bank were created to help poor countries develop from the very beginning.
misconceptions.why: Students project the current stated goals of these institutions onto their historical origins.
misconceptions.fix: These institutions were established at Bretton Woods primarily to manage post-war reconstruction and stabilize international currencies for developed nations.

probe.question: What was the primary purpose of the Bretton Woods institutions?
probe.wrong_answer: To provide financial aid and development funds to poor countries.
